meta.inspiration: A product manager's year in a company with a problem: four quarters, a squad, hidden facts that sponsors state wrongly, one market event and a plan for the year after.
meta.rights_note: Original scenario. The company, the people, the product and every number are invented.

company.name: Marigold Pay
company.one_liner: A three-year-old payments app in India with about 6 lakh active users and a sign-up funnel that leaks at identity checks.
company.stage: Series B, making about ₹2 crore a quarter
company.market: India: mobile-first, price-sensitive, with a regulator that reviews identity checks every year
company.business_model: A fee on merchant payments, a share of credit arranged with a partner bank, and small charges on some transfers.
company.product: The consumer app: sign-up, identity verification, payments and bill pay, and a QR code for small shops.
company.role: Product manager for sign-up and activation. Your squad is eight engineers, three designers and two analysts.
company.brief: You report to the Head of Product and the chief executive sits in your quarterly reviews. Of every hundred people who start signing up, only a handful make a first payment, and the biggest leak is identity verification. The board wants the funnel fixed in a year without hurting the profit. Nobody can say exactly where people drop out, because the app records installs and payments and little in between. You have four quarters of twelve weeks.

stakeholders.name: Meera Joshi
stakeholders.says: Show me what you learned before you show me what you built. In every review I will ask which cause you believe is behind the leak, and why.

stakeholders.name: Arjun Bhatt
stakeholders.says: Merchants will love the soundbox. I met three of them at a fair and they did not want to give it back.

stakeholders.name: Kavya Rao
stakeholders.says: Rivals pay people to join. A first-payment reward and a referral programme will move the number this quarter.

stakeholders.name: Sameer Qureshi
stakeholders.says: If people pay before they are verified, fraud will rise. By how much depends on how many we let through.

stakeholders.name: Tanvi Desai
stakeholders.says: Every change to the identity service takes twice as long as it should. Give us time to clean it.

stakeholders.name: Rohan Iyer
stakeholders.says: Most verification complaints are people who could not get the camera to read the card.

stakeholders.name: The partner bank and the regulator
stakeholders.says: We watch your failure rate. The regulator reviews identity every year.

segments.name: New-to-digital payers
segments.description: People new to digital payments, often on cheap phones and in regional languages.

segments.name: Salaried urban users
segments.description: Salaried people in cities who already pay bills online.

segments.name: Micro-merchants
segments.description: Small shop owners who take payments through a QR code.

items.name: Identity-check camera guidance and retry
items.about: Guided capture for the identity photo: framing hints, glare warnings, one automatic retry.

items.name: Verify after the first payment
items.about: Let people make a first payment before verification finishes, with a low limit until it does.

items.name: First-payment reward
items.about: A small cashback on the first successful payment.

items.name: Regional-language onboarding
items.about: Onboarding and error messages in six regional languages.

items.name: Support deflection assistant
items.about: An assistant that answers the twenty commonest support questions without a person.

items.name: Salary-account linking and credit offers
items.about: Link a salary account and offer credit against it. Needs the partner bank's confidence.

items.name: Merchant QR soundbox integration
items.about: Integrate a QR speaker so merchants hear each payment. Marigold subsidises the device, about ₹1,800 for each of its 46,000 merchants. The chief executive's favourite.

items.name: Fraud rules engine v2
items.about: A rules engine that scores each payment before it clears. Needed before verification can be deferred safely.

items.name: Low-end Android performance
items.about: Make the app fast on 2 GB phones: smaller bundles, fewer cold starts.

items.name: Smart nudges
items.about: Timely reminders to finish verification and to make a first payment.

items.name: Referral programme
items.about: Pay a user and their friend when the friend makes a first payment.

items.name: Funnel event instrumentation
items.about: Record every step of the funnel as events, so the team can see where people leave. Raises measurement to level 2.

items.name: Identity-service refactor
items.about: Rebuild the identity service that every release has to work around. Pays down technical debt.

hidden.label: Share of verification failures that are the camera step
hidden.description: Of the people who fail identity verification, the share who fail at the camera step rather than at document rules or mismatches. Support says most of it is the camera.

hidden.label: Fraud losses if verification is deferred, against today's
hidden.description: Fraud losses, as a multiple of today's, if people can pay before verification finishes. The risk team's number was made when the plan was a small pilot.

hidden.label: Share of rewarded users who leave once the reward is spent
hidden.description: The share of people who take the first-payment reward and leave once it is spent. Growth's figure comes from a campaign that targeted loyal users.

hidden.label: How much merchants value the soundbox, against what is expected
hidden.description: How much merchants really value the soundbox, as a share of the benefit the chief executive expects. Taken from three merchants they met.

events.name: The regulator tightens identity rules
events.signal: Verification completions fell across every segment in one week, and the compliance desk has a new circular.
events.body: A new rule requires a second identity factor. Completion drops until the flow is rebuilt around it.

directions.label: Rebuild to the new rule at once

events.name: The partner bank has a bad week
events.signal: Payments are timing out and support tickets say money left accounts and did not arrive.
events.body: The partner bank's settlement rail fails twice. Users who were mid-payment lose trust in you, not in the bank.

causes.label: Fraud controls are blocking real payments

directions.label: Fail over and tell users plainly

events.name: A rival starts a cashback war
events.signal: New installs are cheaper for the rival and our newest users are leaving for it within weeks.
events.body: A funded rival pays people to switch. The users you are least able to keep are the ones who leave first.

causes.label: A rival is paying to win users

directions.label: Keep our best users, do not match the offer

plans.name: Acquire hard
plans.pitch: Spend heavily on installs next year and live with what it costs.

plans.name: Deepen the base
plans.pitch: Earn more from the people you already have: credit, merchants, fewer exits.

plans.name: Profit first
plans.pitch: Cut acquisition spend and cost to serve, and let the base run.

root.prompt: Which of these do you believe is behind the leak?

options.label: People fail the identity camera step
The identity flow asks too much
There is no reason to make a first payment

measurement.label: Installs and payments
measurement.shows: Arrivals, first payments, customers and the money. Nothing in between.

measurement.label: Core events
measurement.shows: Also sign-ups and the share of customers lost each quarter.

measurement.label: The full funnel
measurement.shows: Also every step and every conversion rate, by segment.
